title: The nine that went back
client: Two parties who are commissioning this together and do not agree. The Harnwell Museum's board, through its keeper of collections, and a delegation of six from the community the nine objects were taken from, who have travelled here twice and who now hold the objects. The keeper signs the cheque. The delegation has a veto that the keeper agreed to in writing and has since asked twice to have clarified.
event: Nine objects, held here since 1907, went home in June after a claim that took eleven years and two refusals. The room they were in has been closed since. It reopens on 14 October with the objects gone and the cases still in it. The museum has never returned anything before and has forty thousand objects acquired in the same decade by the same means.
when: The room reopens 14 October. The objects left on 2 June.
where: The south room of the Harnwell Museum, which is the room they were in.
function: Make the absence do something other than read as a gap. A visitor who came for the nine has to leave knowing they are gone, who has them, and that this was a claim that was resisted for eleven years, not a gift. It has worked if that visitor can say those three things at the door. It has not worked if they leave feeling that the museum has behaved well.
audience: Around nine hundred people a week, two thirds of them school groups aged eight to thirteen with a worksheet, most of whom have been brought here before. Also the regular visitors who know the room and will notice the cases are empty, the delegation's own people who will come to see how it was done, and the keeper's colleagues at four other institutions with claims outstanding against them.
production: Whatever the museum's own workshop can make in six weeks, using the one process they have in the building. No outside supplier, because a purchase order over two thousand goes to the board and the board is where this gets softened.
quantity: One, for the room. If it works the delegation want a second made the same way to go back with them.
mustAppear: the date the room reopens, 14 October
the room it is in, the south room
the length of the claim, eleven years
budget: Four thousand two hundred, from the interpretation line, which is the only line the keeper can spend without the board.
timeline: Installed by 7 October so the education team can rewrite the worksheet. Six weeks from now.
clientWantThatHurtsTheWork: The keeper wants the museum's conduct in the return to be legible on the piece. She is the person who fought the board for eleven years and she is not willing for this to read as an institution being shamed into something.

The delegation will not permit any image of the nine objects to be used. The museum still holds the photographs and still owns the rights, and using them would be the museum exercising, on this of all things, the last piece of ownership it has left.
Nothing that could be read as an instruction to other claimants. Four institutions with live claims are watching and the board has told the keeper that this must not become a campaign.
The trustees' names, or at minimum the museum's own name, on the object itself. The board approved the return and considers that a decision it made.
clientFear: The keeper is afraid it will be read as an apology, which the board would accept and the delegation would find insulting. The delegation is afraid it will be read as a gift, which is what the museum's own account has always implied and what eleven years were spent refusing.
stakes: Forty thousand objects in the same building were acquired the same way, and four other institutions are watching what happens when one of them does this. The nine are already home; what is at issue is whether the return is recorded as a claim that was won or as a kindness that was performed.

hard_constraints.why: Without the number this is about absence in general. Nine is a countable claim that was made and answered, and it is the fact a visitor can carry out of the room.
The date makes it an event that happened rather than a condition that obtains. A room that has always been like this is a room nobody did anything to.
The length of the claim is the difference between a return and a gift, and it is the single fact the museum's own account has always left out.

notes: The keeper has said she will not sign off anything the delegation has not seen first. She has not told the board that.
